cards.front: What are the three steps of platelet plug formation, and which molecules drive each step?
cards.back: **Adhesion**: **vWF** links exposed subendothelial collagen to platelet **GpIb**. **Activation**: platelets release **ADP** and make **TXA2**, which recruit more platelets. **Aggregation**: **fibrinogen** bridges **GpIIb/IIIa** receptors on neighboring platelets.
cards.back_pt: **Adesão**: o **fator de von Willebrand (FvW)** liga o colágeno subendotelial exposto à **GpIb** da plaqueta. **Ativação**: as plaquetas liberam **ADP** e produzem **TXA2**, que recrutam mais plaquetas. **Agregação**: o **fibrinogênio** faz ponte entre receptores **GpIIb/IIIa** de plaquetas vizinhas.

cards.front: Which clotting factors does the PT test, and which does the aPTT test?
cards.back: **PT**: the extrinsic pathway (**factor VII**) plus the common pathway (X, V, II, fibrinogen). **aPTT**: the intrinsic pathway (**XII, XI, IX, VIII**) plus the common pathway. A defect in the common pathway prolongs **both**.
cards.back_pt: **TP**: via extrínseca (**fator VII**) mais a via comum (X, V, II, fibrinogênio). **TTPa**: via intrínseca (**XII, XI, IX, VIII**) mais a via comum. Um defeito na via comum prolonga **ambos**.

cards.front: What causes immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), and what does the bone marrow show?
cards.back: **IgG autoantibodies**, most often against platelet **GpIIb/IIIa**; splenic macrophages remove the coated platelets. **Isolated thrombocytopenia**; PT and aPTT are normal. Marrow shows **more megakaryocytes**. Children: acute, after a viral infection, self-limited. Adults: usually chronic.
cards.back_pt: **Autoanticorpos IgG**, geralmente contra a **GpIIb/IIIa** plaquetária; os macrófagos do baço removem as plaquetas recobertas. **Trombocitopenia isolada**; TP e TTPa normais. A medula mostra **mais megacariócitos**. Crianças: aguda, após infecção viral, autolimitada. Adultos: geralmente crônica.

cards.front: What is the mechanism of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP)?
cards.back: Low **ADAMTS13** activity (usually from an autoantibody) leaves **ultra-large vWF multimers** uncut. Platelets clump in small vessels: **thrombocytopenia**, **schistocytes** (hemolytic anemia), fever, **neurologic** and renal signs. PT and aPTT are **normal**.
cards.back_pt: A baixa atividade da **ADAMTS13** (geralmente por autoanticorpo) deixa **multímeros ultragrandes de FvW** sem clivagem. As plaquetas se agregam em pequenos vasos: **trombocitopenia**, **esquizócitos** (anemia hemolítica), febre, sinais **neurológicos** e renais. TP e TTPa são **normais**.

cards.front: Why does heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) cause clots instead of bleeding?
cards.back: **IgG** binds **heparin–platelet factor 4 (PF4)** complexes and **activates** platelets. Platelets are consumed, so the count falls (typically 5-10 days after starting heparin), and the activated platelets cause **arterial and venous thrombosis**.
cards.back_pt: Anticorpos **IgG** se ligam a complexos **heparina–fator plaquetário 4 (PF4)** e **ativam** as plaquetas. As plaquetas são consumidas, por isso a contagem cai (tipicamente 5 a 10 dias após iniciar a heparina), e as plaquetas ativadas causam **trombose arterial e venosa**.

cards.front: How do Bernard-Soulier syndrome and Glanzmann thrombasthenia differ?
cards.back: **Bernard-Soulier**: **GpIb** deficiency, so platelets cannot **adhere** to vWF; **low count** with **giant platelets**. **Glanzmann**: **GpIIb/IIIa** deficiency, so platelets cannot **aggregate**; normal count and size. Both prolong the **bleeding time**.
cards.back_pt: **Bernard-Soulier**: deficiência de **GpIb**, então as plaquetas não **aderem** ao FvW; **contagem baixa** com **plaquetas gigantes**. **Glanzmann**: deficiência de **GpIIb/IIIa**, então as plaquetas não **agregam**; contagem e tamanho normais. Ambas prolongam o **tempo de sangramento**.

cards.front: What is the defect in factor V Leiden?
cards.back: A point mutation makes factor V **resistant to activated protein C**, so factor Va stays active longer and favors **venous thrombosis**. It is the **most common inherited thrombophilia** in people of European descent. PT and aPTT are normal.
cards.back_pt: Uma mutação pontual torna o fator V **resistente à proteína C ativada**, então o fator Va permanece ativo por mais tempo e favorece **trombose venosa**. É a **trombofilia hereditária mais comum** em pessoas de ascendência europeia. TP e TTPa são normais.

cards.front: Which factors depend on vitamin K, and why does vitamin K deficiency prolong the PT first?
cards.back: The liver needs **vitamin K** to carboxylate factors **II, VII, IX, X** and **proteins C and S**. Factor **VII** has the **shortest half-life**, so it falls first and the **PT** rises before the aPTT. Causes: **newborns**, broad-spectrum antibiotics, fat malabsorption.
cards.back_pt: O fígado precisa da **vitamina K** para carboxilar os fatores **II, VII, IX, X** e as **proteínas C e S**. O fator **VII** tem a **meia-vida mais curta**, então cai primeiro e o **TP** sobe antes do TTPa. Causas: **recém-nascidos**, antibióticos de amplo espectro, má absorção de gorduras.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a swollen, painful right knee after a minor fall while playing. He had a similar episode in his left ankle last year. His maternal uncle had frequent joint bleeds. The knee is warm and tense, and aspiration shows blood. Platelet count is 260,000/mm3, bleeding time is normal, PT is normal, and aPTT is prolonged. The aPTT corrects when his plasma is mixed with normal plasma. Deficiency of which protein is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Joint bleeding (**hemarthrosis**) in a boy with an affected maternal uncle suggests an **X-linked** factor disorder: **hemophilia A** (factor VIII). An isolated long **aPTT** that corrects on mixing points to an intrinsic factor deficiency; hemophilia B (factor IX) looks the same, and only a factor assay separates them. von Willebrand disease can prolong the aPTT, but it causes mucosal bleeding and a prolonged bleeding time. Factor XII deficiency prolongs the aPTT but does not cause bleeding.
questions.explanation_pt: Sangramento articular (**hemartrose**) em um menino com tio materno afetado sugere um distúrbio de fator **ligado ao X**: **hemofilia A** (fator VIII). Um **TTPa** prolongado isolado que corrige no teste de mistura indica deficiência de um fator da via intrínseca; a hemofilia B (fator IX) tem o mesmo quadro, e só a dosagem dos fatores as diferencia. A doença de von Willebrand pode prolongar o TTPa, mas causa sangramento mucoso e tempo de sangramento prolongado. A deficiência de fator XII prolonga o TTPa, mas não causa sangramento.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman comes to the clinic because of heavy menstrual periods since menarche. She has frequent nosebleeds, and she bled for two days after a tooth extraction. Her mother has similar symptoms. She takes no medications. Exam shows a few bruises on her arms and no joint abnormalities. Platelet count is 240,000/mm3 with normal platelet size on the smear. Bleeding time is prolonged, PT is normal, and aPTT is mildly prolonged. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Mucosal bleeding, a dominant family pattern, a **prolonged bleeding time** with a **normal platelet count**, and a mildly long **aPTT** fit **von Willebrand disease**, the most common inherited bleeding disorder. vWF is needed for platelet adhesion and also **protects factor VIII**, which explains the aPTT. Glanzmann thrombasthenia also gives a long bleeding time with a normal count, but the aPTT is normal. Bernard-Soulier causes low counts and giant platelets.
questions.explanation_pt: Sangramento mucoso, padrão familiar dominante, **tempo de sangramento prolongado** com **contagem plaquetária normal** e **TTPa** levemente prolongado indicam **doença de von Willebrand**, o distúrbio hemorrágico hereditário mais comum. O FvW é necessário para a adesão plaquetária e também **protege o fator VIII**, o que explica o TTPa. A trombastenia de Glanzmann também prolonga o tempo de sangramento com contagem normal, mas o TTPa é normal. A síndrome de Bernard-Soulier causa contagem baixa e plaquetas gigantes.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit with a urinary tract infection. Blood cultures grow gram-negative rods. On day 2, blood oozes from his IV sites and he has new petechiae on his legs. Blood pressure is 84/50 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min. Platelet count is 45,000/mm3 (it was 210,000/mm3 on admission). PT and aPTT are both prolonged, fibrinogen is low, and D-dimer is markedly elevated. A blood smear shows schistocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Sepsis triggers widespread activation of coagulation that **consumes** platelets, clotting factors and **fibrinogen**, so PT and aPTT are both long. Fibrin breakdown raises **D-dimer**, and fibrin strands in small vessels cut red cells into **schistocytes**: this is **DIC**. TTP and HUS also cause thrombocytopenia with schistocytes, but PT, aPTT and fibrinogen stay normal. Vitamin K deficiency prolongs the PT (and, when severe, the aPTT), but it does not lower platelets or fibrinogen.
questions.explanation_pt: A sepse desencadeia ativação disseminada da coagulação que **consome** plaquetas, fatores de coagulação e **fibrinogênio**, por isso TP e TTPa estão prolongados. A degradação da fibrina eleva o **dímero-D**, e filamentos de fibrina em pequenos vasos fragmentam as hemácias em **esquizócitos**: trata-se de **CIVD**. A PTT e a SHU também causam trombocitopenia com esquizócitos, mas TP, TTPa e fibrinogênio permanecem normais. A deficiência de vitamina K prolonga o TP (e, se grave, o TTPa), mas não reduz plaquetas nem fibrinogênio.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with a painful, swollen left calf. Ultrasound shows a deep vein thrombosis. She has had two pregnancy losses in the second trimester. She has no bleeding history and takes no medications. Platelet count is 210,000/mm3 and PT is normal. aPTT is prolonged and does not correct when her plasma is mixed with normal plasma. What is the most likely cause of her condition?
questions.explanation: Venous thrombosis plus **recurrent pregnancy loss** suggests **antiphospholipid syndrome**. The **lupus anticoagulant** prolongs the aPTT in the test tube, and the long aPTT that **does not correct on mixing** shows an inhibitor, not a factor deficiency; in the body it causes clotting. A factor VIII inhibitor also fails to correct, but it causes bleeding, not thrombosis. Factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A and protein C deficiency cause clots with a normal aPTT.
questions.explanation_pt: Trombose venosa com **perdas gestacionais de repetição** sugere **síndrome antifosfolípide**. O **anticoagulante lúpico** prolonga o TTPa no tubo de ensaio, e o TTPa prolongado que **não corrige no teste de mistura** indica um inibidor, e não deficiência de fator; no organismo, ele causa trombose. Um inibidor do fator VIII também não corrige, mas causa sangramento, e não trombose. O fator V de Leiden, a mutação G20210A da protrombina e a deficiência de proteína C causam trombose com TTPa normal.

notes.title: Hemostasis and coagulation: lab patterns and key disorders
notes.body_md:
## Normal hemostasis

- **Vasoconstriction**, then a **platelet plug**: adhesion (vWF–GpIb), activation (ADP, TXA2), aggregation (fibrinogen–GpIIb/IIIa).
- **Coagulation** builds a fibrin mesh. **Vitamin K** is needed to make factors **II, VII, IX, X** and **proteins C and S**.
- Natural brakes: **antithrombin** (inhibits thrombin and Xa), **proteins C and S** (inactivate Va and VIIIa), **TFPI** (blocks tissue factor–VIIa).
- **Fibrinolysis**: **tPA** converts plasminogen to **plasmin**, which cuts fibrin; **α2-antiplasmin** inhibits plasmin. **D-dimer** is a fibrin breakdown product.

## Reading the lab pattern

- **Platelet disorders** (ITP, TTP, Bernard-Soulier, Glanzmann): long **bleeding time**, normal PT and aPTT; mucosal bleeding and petechiae.
- **Hemophilia A (VIII) or B (IX)**: X-linked recessive; only the **aPTT** is long; deep bleeding such as **hemarthrosis**.
- **von Willebrand disease**: the most common inherited bleeding disorder; long bleeding time, aPTT normal or long. **Desmopressin** releases stored vWF.
- **Vitamin K deficiency** (newborns, antibiotics, malabsorption) and **liver disease**: the **PT** rises first (factor VII has the shortest half-life), then the aPTT.
- **DIC** (sepsis, obstetric emergencies, cancer, trauma): low platelets, long PT and aPTT, low **fibrinogen**, high **D-dimer**, **schistocytes**.
- **HUS**: schistocytes and kidney injury, usually after Shiga toxin diarrhea (see the GI infections block).

## Mixing study

- Patient plasma is mixed with normal plasma. **Correction** means a factor deficiency. **No correction** means an **inhibitor** (lupus anticoagulant or an anti-factor VIII antibody).

## Thrombophilias

- **Factor V Leiden** (most common inherited), **prothrombin G20210A**, **protein C or S deficiency**, and **antithrombin deficiency** (poor response to heparin).
- **Antiphospholipid syndrome**: arterial and venous clots and **recurrent pregnancy loss**; the lupus anticoagulant prolongs the aPTT in vitro; may cause a false-positive VDRL.
- **Virchow triad**: stasis, endothelial injury and hypercoagulability. For anticoagulant drugs, see the pharmacology block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Hemostasia normal

- **Vasoconstrição**, depois o **tampão plaquetário**: adesão (FvW–GpIb), ativação (ADP, TXA2), agregação (fibrinogênio–GpIIb/IIIa).
- A **coagulação** forma uma rede de fibrina. A **vitamina K** é necessária para produzir os fatores **II, VII, IX, X** e as **proteínas C e S**.
- Freios naturais: **antitrombina** (inibe trombina e Xa), **proteínas C e S** (inativam Va e VIIIa), **TFPI** (bloqueia fator tecidual–VIIa).
- **Fibrinólise**: o **tPA** converte plasminogênio em **plasmina**, que cliva a fibrina; a **alfa-2-antiplasmina** inibe a plasmina. O **dímero-D** é um produto de degradação da fibrina.

## Interpretando o padrão laboratorial

- **Distúrbios plaquetários** (PTI, PTT, Bernard-Soulier, Glanzmann): **tempo de sangramento** prolongado, TP e TTPa normais; sangramento mucoso e petéquias.
- **Hemofilia A (VIII) ou B (IX)**: recessiva ligada ao X; só o **TTPa** é prolongado; sangramento profundo, como **hemartrose**.
- **Doença de von Willebrand**: o distúrbio hemorrágico hereditário mais comum; tempo de sangramento prolongado, TTPa normal ou prolongado. A **desmopressina** libera o FvW armazenado.
- **Deficiência de vitamina K** (recém-nascidos, antibióticos, má absorção) e **doença hepática**: o **TP** sobe primeiro (o fator VII tem a meia-vida mais curta), depois o TTPa.
- **CIVD** (sepse, emergências obstétricas, câncer, trauma): plaquetas baixas, TP e TTPa prolongados, **fibrinogênio** baixo, **dímero-D** alto, **esquizócitos**.
- **SHU**: esquizócitos e lesão renal, geralmente após diarreia por toxina Shiga (ver o bloco de infecções gastrointestinais).

## Teste de mistura

- O plasma do paciente é misturado com plasma normal. **Correção** indica deficiência de fator. **Ausência de correção** indica um **inibidor** (anticoagulante lúpico ou anticorpo antifator VIII).

## Trombofilias

- **Fator V de Leiden** (a hereditária mais comum), **mutação G20210A da protrombina**, **deficiência de proteína C ou S** e **deficiência de antitrombina** (**resistência à heparina**).
- **Síndrome antifosfolípide**: tromboses arteriais e venosas e **perdas gestacionais de repetição**; o anticoagulante lúpico prolonga o TTPa in vitro; pode causar VDRL falso-positivo.
- **Tríade de Virchow**: estase, lesão endotelial e hipercoagulabilidade. Para os anticoagulantes, ver o bloco de farmacologia.
